title: Per-tenant memory bartering for micro-burst resilience
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Persistent micro-bursts from mixed-priority tenants frequently drive transient KV/activation pressure that leads to tail latency spikes or reactive OOM-driven evictions. Current soft-reservation model is overly conservative (high wasted headroom) or too brittle (preemptive evictions for lower-priority tenants). Goal: design and ship a per-tenant 'memory bartering' layer that lets tenants temporarily borrow unused headroom from others under explicit credit accounting, with a progressive spill/fallback so we avoid hard OOMs while preserving latency SLOs.

Key constraints and goals:
- Keep weight memory pinned where possible; only KV + activations are candidates for dynamic barter/spill.
- Avoid cross-tenant data leakage: barter is strictly capacity accounting, not data sharing.
- Maintain predictable p50/p95 tail-latency for P0/P1 tenants.
- Minimize long-term headroom waste while improving micro-burst acceptance.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Per-tenant memory credit ledger: each tenant has a credit balance derived from reserved capacity and historical usage. Credits increase slowly when a tenant consistently under-uses its reservation; credits are consumed during micro-bursts. Credits decay over a configurable window to prevent hoarding.
2) Borrowing policy: when a tenant exceeds its active reservation, the runtime consults the ledger and allows borrowing up to X% of global available credits subject to conservative caps and priority buckets. Borrowed memory is tagged for accounting and eligible for prioritized reclamation.
3) Progressive spill hierarchy: (a) prefix/KV compression & compaction, (b) KV spill-to-host-ram (NUMA aware), (c) KV spill-to-NVMe with async prefetch hints, (d) activation checkpoint-to-host. Each step prefers non-blocking operations with predictive prefetch when we detect repayment intent.
4) Continuous-batching integration: borrowing decisions are made per-batch window; the batcher will adjust batch size heuristics to reduce future borrow pressure (e.g., smaller batches for bursty tenants).
5) Telemetry & safety: emit granular events (borrow-grant, borrow-repay, spill-step, reclaimed) and surface a 'barter health' dashboard. Automatic circuit-breaker when global reclaim rate exceeds threshold or when borrow repayment rate drops below target.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bench: under synthetic micro-burst traffic (10x baseline qps for 2s windows across 20% tenants), 99.5% of requests succeed without fallback model and p95 latency increases by <30% compared to steady baseline.
- No new OOM incidents in canary when running mixed-workload tests for 48 hours.
- Telemetry shows borrow repay rate > 90% and average borrow latency < 5ms accounting ops.
- Feature guarded by FF and disabled by default on existing clusters.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Accounting overhead may add CPU latency to hot-pathed request admission. Mitigation: batch accounting updates and use lock-free counters.
- Excessive borrowing could mask chronic under-provisioning. Mitigation: slow credit accumulation and auto-alerts for long-term imbalance.
- Spill-to-NVMe adds tail latency for first miss; mitigate with async prefetch and conservative thresholds.

Instrumentation & tests:
- Unit: ledger ops, decay window, priority enforcement.
- Integration: local multi-GPU cluster with synthetic tenants and NVMe backing; validate spill/prefetch paths.
- Perf: 1k-tenant stressbench (existing harness) with detailed per-tenant memory traces.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge ledger skeleton behind FF (internal only).
2) Canary in dedicated-qa with conservative caps (10% global borrow).
3) Expand to 10% of Dedicated capacity and run 48h soak.
4) Ramp to standard dedicated clusters with alerting and revert FF if reclaim rate < 80% or OOMs observed.

Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/Memory+Bartering+Design
Perf dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/memory-bartering-canary
comments: 2026-02-21 — Avery Chen: Initial spike investigation and proposal. Attached first-pass ledger design and cost model in Confluence. Noted that weights must remain pinned; only KV and activations are candidates.
2026-02-26 — Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed. Ask: make priority buckets explicit and ensure SLOs for tier-1 customers are unbreakable. Suggest adding repayment SLAs and alerting for persistent borrowers.

2026-03-01 — Diego Morales: Prototype ledger implemented (in-memory, sharded). Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4271. Bench harness updated to emit per-tenant borrow events.

2026-03-03 — Design review: Miguel Alvarez (SRE) flagged concern about NVMe spill rate and prefetched hotspot thrash. Decision: add per-device spill queue and throttle prefetch concurrency. Follow-up ticket created for NVMe prefetch queue tuning.

2026-03-07 — Benchmark results (canary): With 10% global borrow cap, average borrow repay rate = 93%, p95 latency delta = +18% during 2s bursts. CPU overhead for accounting ~1.2%. Logging and metrics look stable. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/memory-bartering-canary?panelId=2
2026-03-09 — Security review (informal): No tenant data movement, only capacity accounting. Formal review skipped but will add to quarterly compliance sweep.
